questions.prompt: What is Beany worried about for the science fair?
choices: That Kevin will not be a good partner.
That their experiment will not get a good grade.
That Ms. Babbitt will be angry with them.
That they will run out of supplies.
questions.evidenceSnippet: But Beany is worried that their experiment will not get a good grade. Some of the other students are making glittery posters. Others are going to play music. Kevin insists that all they need is good science. How can they compete without fancy props?
questions.evidenceHighlight: Beany is worried that their experiment will not get a good grade.

questions.evidenceSnippet: On the day of the science fair, I woke up early, before the alarm went off. I lay in bed hugging Jingle Bell and worrying.

questions.prompt: True or False: Carol Ann and Stacy were worried about their science project.
questions.evidenceSnippet: In the bus that morning, I saw that Carol Ann and Stacy were dressed alike. Carol Ann and Stacy didn't seem worried. They were talking nonstop about how much fun the science fair was going to be.
questions.evidenceHighlight: Carol Ann and Stacy didn't seem worried.

questions.prompt: What did Beany want to add to her project after seeing other projects?
questions.evidenceSnippet: When I saw the volcano, I ran back to our table. 'Kevin, you should see the volcano. It's huge. Why didn't we think of a volcano?' ... 'Carol Ann and Stacy have streamers all around the edge of their table. Why didn't we think of that?' ... 'Manuel and Boomer are doing a planet project, and they have a black tablecloth with stars all over it. Why didn't we use a cool tablecloth instead of a dumb white one with a gravy stain on it?'
questions.evidenceHighlight: Why didn't we think of a volcano?

'Look at all those balloons! Balloons are better than bubbles! How come we only have one itsy-bitsy one in our project?'
